summary: This resolution sets expedited House floor procedures for three bills by waiving points of order, automatically adopting committee substitutes, limiting debate to one hour per bill, and allowing one motion to recommit, while also excluding certain days from counting toward termination of specified national emergencies.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural, setting debate rules for three underlying bills. It contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any government spending.
No tax provisions, rate changes, or revenue measures appear in the text of the resolution.
The resolution does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.

Section 1 sets the terms for floor consideration of H.R. 2189, a bill whose title explicitly concerns modernization of federal firearms laws. While the resolution itself is procedural, it directly enables debate on legislation that engages gun policy.
No immigration-related content is present.
No provisions touch abortion access or restrictions.
The resolution contains no defense or military spending language.

Section 2 enables consideration of H.R. 261, which amends the National Marine Sanctuaries Act regarding undersea cables. This touches environmental regulatory procedures in marine sanctuaries, creating a tangential link.
No welfare, entitlement, or safety-net provisions exist.
The resolution does not engage education policy.
No drug-policy content is present.
No criminal-justice or sentencing provisions appear.
The resolution does not address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No debt, deficit, or fiscal-target language is included.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
Foreign aid is not mentioned.
The resolution does not alter voting procedures or election rules.
No technology, data, or privacy regulation is addressed.
Labor or union issues are absent.
